religion_note: China Family Panel Studies 2016 adult questionnaire, religious affiliation (qm601) by province, tabulated with the wave's cross-sectional individual weight (rswt_natcs16) from the public-release file. A survey of adults, not a census: China's census does not ask religion. Self-declared affiliation, 3,786 respondents in this province, which CFPS draws as an independent, self-representative subsample -- one of five provinces (Shanghai, Liaoning, Henan, Gansu, Guangdong) for which the survey supports province-level inference; the other provinces are not written. Weighted by rswt_natcs16, counting the 3,786 respondents who carry it. The same reading of the 2012 file, unweighted, reproduces Table 2 of Lu Yunfeng's report (https://web.archive.org/web/20140809051625/http://iwr.cass.cn/zjwh/201403/W020140303370398758556.pdf) within 0.5 points in every share, which is how the province codes are known to be right; that published table is unweighted, so it and this figure differ by the weight and not by the data. The 2016 questionnaire asks which religion a person believes in (信仰) where 2012 asked which they belong to (属于), and allows more than one answer, of which the first is counted; shares rose in every province between the two waves, and part of that rise is the wording. Affiliation, not practice.

religion_note: China Family Panel Studies 2016 adult questionnaire, religious affiliation (qm601) by province, tabulated with the wave's cross-sectional individual weight (rswt_natcs16) from the public-release file. A survey of adults, not a census: China's census does not ask religion. Self-declared affiliation, 2,775 respondents in this province, which CFPS draws as an independent, self-representative subsample -- one of five provinces (Shanghai, Liaoning, Henan, Gansu, Guangdong) for which the survey supports province-level inference; the other provinces are not written. Weighted by rswt_natcs16, counting the 2,775 respondents who carry it. The same reading of the 2012 file, unweighted, reproduces Table 2 of Lu Yunfeng's report (https://web.archive.org/web/20140809051625/http://iwr.cass.cn/zjwh/201403/W020140303370398758556.pdf) within 0.5 points in every share, which is how the province codes are known to be right; that published table is unweighted, so it and this figure differ by the weight and not by the data. The 2016 questionnaire asks which religion a person believes in (信仰) where 2012 asked which they belong to (属于), and allows more than one answer, of which the first is counted; shares rose in every province between the two waves, and part of that rise is the wording. Affiliation, not practice.

sources.name: National Bureau of Statistics of China, Seventh National Population Census (2020), population by ethnic group

adapter_hint: CFPS 2012 (religion) for the five provinces the survey sampled on their own, transcribed from Lu Yunfeng's report: python -m scripts.fetch_census.cfps_survey; census ethnicity by province, transcribed in each province's Wikipedia article: python -m scripts.fetch_census.china_wiki. Hong Kong SAR carries ethnicity and usual spoken language from its own 2021 Population Census (C&SD Main Results, Tables 3.9 and 3.13): python -m scripts.fetch_census.hongkong_census. Macau SAR carries nationality (as ethnicity, labelled nationality) and usual language from its own 2021 Population Census (DSEC Detailed Results, Tables 6 and 10): python -m scripts.fetch_census.macau_census
ethnicity_note: National Bureau of Statistics of China, Seventh National Population Census (2020), population by ethnic group, resident population of Tibet Autonomous Region, as the English Wikipedia article 'List of Chinese administrative divisions by ethnic group' transcribes it. Shares computed from the printed counts. The table lists the region's largest nationalities; the 26,373 residents it does not name are written as 'Other ethnic groups' with its own residual rows ('Undistinguished').

name: Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region

religion.note: China's census does not ask religion; it records the 56 official nationalities (minzu) instead. The China Family Panel Studies asked it in 2012 and supports province-level figures for five provinces (Shanghai, Liaoning, Henan, Gansu, Guangdong), which carry them.
